newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF REAL BETIS PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF REAL BETIS PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the Real Betis players most likely to feature against Real Madrid in Saturday's Spanish league game:

Toni Prats, goalkeeper, 25. Former Spanish junior international widely seen as future senior side 'keeper. Prats has excelled since joining from Celta in the summer but was blamed for a Roberto Carlos free-kick goal earlier this season.
Pedro Jaro, goalkeeper, 32. The first division's most successful 'keeper after signing from Real Madrid in 1994, Jaro lost his form last season and has been sidelined by the arrival of Prats.

Jaime Quesada, defender, 25. Right back who once grabbed the headlines by scoring the winning goal for lowly Lledia against Barcelona in the Camp Nou. After two good seasons, Jaime has lost his place in the reshaped Betis defence.

Roberto Rios, defender, 25. Defensive giant who has caught the attention of Manchester United and Athletic Bilbao. Strong in the air, Rios plays on the right side of the defence but is a natural goalscorer coming forward at set pieces.
Tomas Olias, defender, 28. Left back who joined Betis four years ago in an exchange deal with Marbella. One of the surprises of the season, he has scored four vital goals away from home.
Juan Urena, defender, 29. A veteran from Betis' dark years in the second division, Urena's career has been plagued with injuries and he is an unlikely starter.
Hristo Vidakovic, defender, 28. Bosnian-born central defender who will be given the job of controlling fellow Yugoslavian international Predrag Mijatovic.
Juan Merino, midfielder/defender, 26. A former reserve team player who has been moved up from defence into Serra Ferrer's remodelled five-man midfield.

Nenad Bjelica, midfielder, 25. Left-sided Croatian who signed in the close season when it seemed that Jarni would leave Spain. Has hardly played this season because of injury. Scored 13 goals for Albacete last season.
Juan Canas, midfielder, 24. A product of the Betis junior sides, Canas has failed to hold down a regular place this season after a good run last year. Disciplined and hard tackler.
Albert Nadj, midfielder, 22. Right-sided Yugoslav international who has been sidelined by injuries and the presence of Finidi since signing from Partizan Belgrade in the close season.
Alexis Trujillo, midfielder, 31. Club captain and penalty taker, Alexis has been virtually ever-present since joining from Tenerife two seasons ago.

Finidi George, midfielder/striker, 25. Betis beat off a challenge from Real Madrid to sign the Nigerian international winger from Ajax over the close season. Quick and skilful down the right, Finidi is frequently the subject of reckless tackling.

Robert Jarni, midfielder/striker, 28. Left-sided Croatian international who has blossomed this season after seeing a move to England fall through. The former Juventus man crosses well and is a fine set-piece specialist.
Juan Sabas, striker, 29. Diminutive former Atletico Madrid forward who regularly turns round games after coming on as substitute. Could start his first league game this season.

Wojcech Kowalczyk, striker, 24. Polish international who cost a then club-record 400 million pesetas ($2.84 million) when signed from Legia Warsaw in 1994. Is likely to start after scoring four goals in recent matches.
Pier Cherubino, striker, 25. Rome-born former Spanish international, is particularly strong in the air. Will dispute the two places up front with Sabas and Kowalczyk.
